Soft Clay · neurological examination · part 5 of 11

Motor system of the arms: storyboard

Twelve beats, 90 s. Every still is rendered with the STAGE kit from the real scene (shared v5 patient, set and hands, the same cameras and the same solved contact poses the animation uses), at 16 samples, 960×540, the captioned version. Holds (still, no caption, for the speech added later) are listed under each beat.

Step 0: the attachments

  • soft-clay-REFERENCE-STYLE-SOURCE.txt: read whole (372 lines); its code is identical to styles/soft-clay.js. The full prompt (soft-clay-cns-part5-motor-arms-prompt.txt, 2032 lines) was read whole: after MY CONTENT come STORYBOARD FIRST, WHAT TO BUILD, HOW TO STAY IN THE STYLE, FLOW BETWEEN BEATS, SOUND (no voiceover: a fuller mix), the rendering note, STYLE CARD, STAGE KIT, SOUND KIT, TEXT3D and REFERENCE STYLE SOURCE; the kits embedded in it are identical to lib/.
  • series-shared-v5.zip: series/cvs1-style.js; shared/ abdo.js, bed.js, caption.js, clay.js, hands.js, home.js, neuro.js, neuro-props.js, patient.js, patient-neuro.js, props.js, set.js, sheet.js, README.md (contains 'v5: neuro mode'); ref/ patient_full.png, patient_face.png, patient_cns_full.png, patient_cns_face.png (plus patient_flat_full.png and patient_flat_abdomen.png). Everything required is there; shared/ is used unchanged (byte-identical to the zip).
  • lib/stage.js (39688 bytes, md5 980404cad405873f5891ccafbd6e2065), lib/sound.js (22800, 99b0970f88de7265655ccf2a16b5b65c) and lib/text3d.js (54931, c3aa8d0fb28b30af3ebb61a1f631bc4c) come unchanged from part 4 (IT-Ali/clay-cns-4); the zip has no lib/.

Changed in this round

  • Checked against the full prompt: update(t) no longer keeps any state between calls (the examiner's hand used to remember the last arm angles while his arm moved to or from rest; it now uses the fixed test position), so frames are identical in any render order.
  • His arm now holds the test position until the examiner's hand has left it (no arm moving under a hand).
  • Every rustle starts on the exact pose frame of its event (the arm leaving or reaching the mattress), from the same schedule as the picture.
  • Elbow cup (tone): the hand is now searched for its turn on the elbow as well as where it sits (turned 40 deg), and solved at every pose frame his arm takes while the examiner holds it (149 frames; the arm moves on twos, so nothing is blended between solved poses, which before let the fingers sink up to 15 mm into the elbow). The palm cups the back of the elbow and all four fingers wrap round its inner side; every finger PAD rests on the skin (palm 0.50-0.52 mm, fingers 0.15-0.81 mm, pads 0.49-0.81 mm). No finger joint bends past its limit (before, the little finger was curled past 160 deg at the middle joint).
  • Pads: every finger and thumb contact is now also measured at its pad (the end bone), not only at its nearest point, and the solver bends a finger's joints until its pad rests on the skin. This found and fixed the handshake (the examiner's middle finger and his middle and ring fingers had pads 4-6 mm off) and the elbow-flexion thumb (3.2 mm). All 96 pads: 0.05-1.09 mm.
  • Grip: his thumb starts from NEURO.HAND.grip and its two joints are flexed until its pad rests on the gloved fingers: pad 0.05 mm (nearest point 0.00 mm), shown in the side and below panels (e).
  • Cup panel (b): filmed from above the inner side of the elbow, where the fingers wrap (the old camera was inside the mattress).

The beats

Beat 1 · Position0.0 - 5.0 s · still at 4.6 s
Motor system: the arms
Changes
Starts on the CNS home shot, held still for 1 s (no caption, breathing and lamp flicker off). He breathes quietly (about 14 a minute) from then on.
Camera
From the CNS home shot, one slow push-in toward his upper body and both arms.
Sound
Quiet room bed, fading in over the first 0.5 s.
Beat 2 · Inspection5.0 - 13.0 s · hold 5.3-6.8 s · still at 11.3 s
Look: no wasting, no fasciculation, no tremor (ask about pain first)
Changes
Hold (still, no caption: the examiner asks about pain in his arms or shoulders). He answers "no" (silent visemes, 6.85 s). The camera then moves slowly along both arms (7.3-12.7 s): the shoulders and deltoids, the upper arms, the forearms, then the backs of both hands with the first dorsal interosseous. Nothing twitches or shakes; no scars. The examiner's hands stay at rest.
Camera
One continuous move from the foot end above him, along both arms from the shoulders down to the backs of the hands.
Sound
Room only.
Beat 3 · Tone - right arm13.0 - 23.0 s · hold 13.3-14.8 s · still at 16.6 s
Tone: let it go floppy - wrist, forearm, elbow, shoulder: normal
Changes
Hold (the examiner asks him to let the arm go floppy). He offers his right hand; the examiner takes it as in a handshake (palm to palm, the thumb webs together, the examiner's fingers round the little-finger edge onto the back of his hand, the thumbs crossing over the backs of the hands) and cups the back of his elbow with the other palm. From 15.8 s the examiner moves the wrist (flexion and extension), turns the forearm (supination and pronation), bends and straightens the elbow and moves the shoulder out and in, at irregular, changing speeds: smooth and loose, no catch. Released at 21.6 s.
Camera
From his right side, a little above: the whole arm from the shoulder to the hand and both gloved hands.
Sound
A soft rustle as his arm leaves the mattress and comes back.
Beat 4 · Tone - left arm23.0 - 29.6 s · still at 25.6 s
Same on the left: normal tone
Changes
Hard cut to his LEFT at 23.0 s (the examiner has walked round; the gloved hands already at rest on that side, the sleeves leaving the frame on his left). The same handshake and elbow cup on his left arm, the same moves a little faster; then a hard cut back to his right side at 29.6 s.
Camera
Across the bed from his left (never through the bed or the table).
Sound
Rustle as the arm lifts and is put back.
Beat 5 · key beat · Pronator drift29.6 - 42.0 s · hold 29.9-31.4 s · still at 36.0 s
Pronator drift: arms out, palms up, eyes closed - no drift
Changes
THE KEY BEAT. Hold (the examiner asks him to hold both arms out, palms up, and close his eyes). He lifts both arms straight out in front at shoulder height, parallel, palms up, fingers together (NEURO.arm outstretched, drift 0) and closes his eyes (31.5-32.5 s); held still 32.6-39.6 s (7 s): neither arm turns in or drifts down. He opens his eyes and lowers his arms to rest. The examiner's hands stay at rest at his right side.
Camera
From the foot end, a little to his right and a little above shoulder height: both arms full length, both palms and his closed eyes.
Sound
Rustle as the arms leave and return to the mattress.

What I checked in every panel

  • Contacts: every contact is measured on the meshes of the rendered frames (not the intended values), at its nearest point and, for fingers and thumbs, at its pad; the table at the bottom lists each one: the tone contacts (handshake and elbow cup) at every pose frame from the start of the moves until the examiner lets go, the power tests at mid-press. All 114 pass (nearest points 0.00-1.20 mm, pads 0.05-1.09 mm).
  • Hand rules: fingers together in every contact (each finger may turn at most 0.15 rad toward its neighbours to reach the skin), no V (the two gloved fingers of the grip side by side), no upright hand on the bed, no hand on its edge except the pointing hand of finger abduction, whose index comes down onto the side of his finger from above.
  • His RIGHT and LEFT: checked in the plan panel (a); every left-side test is filmed from his left with the examiner on his left (the sleeves leave the frame on that side); the bedside table is on his left near his head and no camera passes through it or the bed.
  • No text in the scene: only the caption plaque (off in the review panels, which carry review labels only).
  • The neck is the kit's slim neck (no change to shared/).
  • Every sign named in a caption can be seen: inspection shows both shoulders, upper arms, forearms and the backs of both hands; drift shows both palms level and his closed eyes; each power panel shows the named point and the examiner's hand.

Facts and choices I had to assume

  • He stays half-sitting at 45 degrees for the whole part (as the brief allows); 'the upper arm resting on the bed by his side' is the upper arm lying along the backrest beside his trunk.
  • Wrist extension: with the trunk at 45 degrees his forearm cannot lie flat on the mattress with the elbow bent, so it lies palm down beside him resting on the examiner's other palm, which steadies it from below; the fist is cocked up from there.
  • Finger flexion: his forearm points forward with the thumb up, so the examiner's two fingers go down through his grip from the thumb side and their tips come out under his little finger.
  • Finger abduction: his hand rests on the front of his thigh (on the pyjama trousers, 10 cm above the knee).
  • Each 'hold' is 1.5 s with the picture still apart from his quiet breathing; his only words are 'no' (beat 2), as silent visemes.
  • The limb gives about 2 mm under the examiner's hand and then holds (shoulder 0.55 deg, elbow 0.6 deg, wrist 1.8 deg, the hand 0.55 deg of elbow, the index finger about 2 mm); the working muscle firms by about 1 mm (no lump). Finger abduction: no firming of the first dorsal interosseous is modelled (it would read as a lump at that size).
  • The kit's fist leaves a see-through loop seen from the thumb side, so this part uses its own fist (the fingers bent more at the middle joints, the thumb across the front of the index and middle fingers); the kit's NEURO.HAND poses are used for the drift (together), the grip and finger abduction (spread).
  • Tone moves: the wrist 45 deg flexion to 38 deg extension, the forearm 72 deg supination to 55 deg pronation, the elbow 28 to 112 deg, the shoulder 4 to 30 deg out, at irregular speeds; the left arm 1.3 times faster.
  • Between beats the view changes by hard cuts that land on him (allowed by the brief's transition rules), and the walk round to his left and back is always a hard cut, as asked; FLOW BETWEEN BEATS' 'no hard cuts' is overridden by MY CONTENT here.
